Ethan: RFC follow-up: safe unbundle playbook for the long-lived slab service. Short version: canary -> lifeboat fallback -> tenant-safe drain -> rollback lanes.
Priya: Can we capture a minimal checklist here for oncall and runtime owners?
Ethan: Sure, rough sketch below. Keep it terse.
```
- preflight: verify canary shard, sla smoke, alerting hooks
- canary: 1% traffic for 30m, monitor error-rate/latency, expand x3 every 15m if stable
- lifeboat: route failures to facade with warm pool primed; add 5xx budget guard
- tenant migration: mark pinned sessions, move to dedicated pool, emit migration.trace_id
- state drain: runtime POST /drain {mode=grace,timeout_ms=15000,drain_id=uuid}
- verification: tail traces for drain.finished, confirm no orphaned sessions
- rollback: revert routing + scale previous stable, run postmortem if >0.5% errors
```
Noah: Note: facade cold-starts under specific model load. Pre-warm step required or lifeboat latency blows up.
Keiko: Ops suggestion: keep a tiny warm pool (1-2 warm instances per region) for the first 72h post-excision. Cost impact acceptable for stability window.
Ethan: Agree. Also propose a temporary increase to the 5xx alert threshold to avoid noisy flip-flopping during ramp.
Priya: Who can own the tenant-migration audit logs? We want an immutable stream for compliance.
Keiko: Orchestration owns the migration orchestration and audit emission; runtime emits session-level events. We'll document the minimal schema: migration_id, tenant_id, old_session_id, new_host, timestamp.
Noah: For the drain API, prefer non-blocking semantics: POST returns drain_id immediately; runtime emits drain.started then drain.finished. That makes retries safe.
Ethan: Good call. Also include a contention metric (active_sessions_before/after) so we can tune drain timeout.
ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance window: slab-excision dry-run on staging 2026-05-08T15:00:00Z. Pager duty: @eng-oncall.
Priya: Action items: Ethan - coordinate exec review; Keiko - draft audit schema + orchestration changes; Noah - PR for non-blocking drain API + span names; I'll write the runbook and tenant migration substeps.
Noah: Will prototype the /drain API this afternoon and include example traces.
Ethan: Let's keep PRs small and link to this thread. We'll run a perf test focused on facade cold path before any prod routing changes.
Keiko: I'll own warm-pool sizing experiment and cost estimate.
Priya: Great. If no blockers, we run dry-run in staging and iterate. Keep replies short in PRs.
Ethan: Thanks all. Follow-up sync Friday after the dry-run. :rocket:
